Rarity.rationale: Matches RazorTooth.cs:11. In the transcribed shared grab bag as Rare (relic_pools.py:123), executed by `py tools/audit/relic_probes_b13.py pool`.

AfterCardPlayed.rationale: RazorTooth.cs:13-30 runs four checks in order -- card owner, card type, IsUpgradable, then CardCmd.Upgrade -- and razor_tooth.py:22 runs the same three conditions before card.upgrade(). Each is verdicted at its own guard (N1-N4); no divergence was found at any of them, so this hook rolls up faithful per binding rule 4. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/relic_probes_b13.py razor-tooth`): a Strike played once comes out at upgrade_level 1 and a second play leaves it at 1 (max_upgrade_level 1), a Dazed and a Burn stay at 0, and the run deck after finish_combat is still [('bash',0),('defend',0),('strike',0)].

guards.what: N1: `(uint)(type - 1) > 1u` (RazorTooth.cs:20) is the decompiler's rendering of 'Attack or Skill'
guards.rationale: CardType is None=0, Attack=1, Skill=2, Power=3, Status=4, Curse=5, Quest=6 (Entities/Cards/CardType.cs:3-12), so `(uint)(type - 1) > 1` early-returns for everything except type 1 and 2. razor_tooth.py:22's `card.card_type in (CardType.ATTACK, CardType.SKILL)` is exactly that set. Recorded because the unsigned-underflow idiom is easy to read as the wrong comparison -- for type == None (0) the subtraction wraps to uint.MaxValue and correctly returns. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardType.cs is not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2 (PROMPT.md bug class 14): `if (!cardPlay.Card.IsUpgradable) return;` (RazorTooth.cs:24-27) IS mirrored -- razor_tooth.py:22 checks card.is_upgradable
guards.rationale: The sim's Card.upgrade() (cards/base.py) is a bare `upgrade_level += 1` with no guard of its own, so every caller must supply one; sweep D found 7 of 23 relic call sites that do not, and two of those (astrolabe, bone_tea) are recorded live gaps. This relic is NOT one of them -- `py tools/audit/relic_probes.py sweep-upgrade` does not list razor_tooth.py, and the guard is executed above: Dazed and Burn (max_upgrade_level 0, the Curse/Status population) come out of on_card_played at upgrade_level 0. Checked rather than assumed, because the relic upgrades a card the player just played and Status cards ARE playable (Burn is not, but Dazed reaches the hand and Slimed is playable).

guards.what: N3: 'for the rest of the combat' -- the upgrade must not reach the run deck
guards.rationale: C# upgrades the combat CardModel instance (CardCmd.Upgrade(cardPlay.Card)); the sim upgrades the combat Card instance. The sim's combat piles are a deepcopy of the run deck (RunState.create_combat, run.py:1136, whose docstring says 'the game clones canonical cards into each combat the same way'), so the upgrade cannot leak. EXECUTED end to end above: after finish_combat the run deck's upgrade levels are all 0 even though the played Strike reached level 1 in combat. NOTE per binding rule 7: run.py is not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4: C# has NO IsAutoPlay exclusion and no IsInProgress guard here
guards.rationale: RazorTooth.cs:13-30's only guards are the three in N1-N2 plus the owner check, so an auto-played Attack is upgraded on both sides -- unlike relic/brilliant_scarf (BrilliantScarf.cs:84-87), whose auto-play exclusion the sim drops as a live gap. Same near-miss as relic/rainbow_ring N1 in this batch. The missing IsInProgress guard is structurally satisfied in the sim: on_card_played is a combat hook and combat.py's play loop breaks once the fight is decided.

guards.what: N5: the relic has no state and no reset hooks at all
guards.rationale: RazorTooth.cs overrides exactly Rarity and AfterCardPlayed -- no BeforeCombatStart, no AfterCombatEnd, no counter -- so PROMPT.md bug class 13 (a dropped per-combat reset) has nothing to bite here, and `py tools/audit/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` puts razor_tooth in the 'relics holding no state at all' bucket. Recorded so the absence is visibly a source property rather than an omission in the port.
